title: Hindsight Memory-PRM: Supervising Memory Management with Auditable Hindsight Credit

visual_explainer.blocker: A paper-specific mechanism figure has not yet passed grounded VISUAL_POLICY.md review; the verified bilingual deep note carries the intervention, matched controls, and lifecycle-cost caveats meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: Hindsight Memory-PRM turns downstream memory use into auditable supervision: retrieval logs, answer citations, and controlled deletion-and-reanswer produce intervention-calibrated credit for Write/Merge/Noop decisions. Its strongest evidence is a same-scaffold ladder that separates sparse outcome reward, observational attribution, and intervention information under a fixed reader.
analysis.problem: Long-horizon memory managers take dozens of Write, Merge, or Noop decisions before an episode-level answer reward arrives, so outcome-only RL gives nearly every operation the same delayed credit and makes it hard to tell which memory action later mattered.
analysis.core_idea: Log every memory operation and read path, certify zero contribution for entries never touched by retrieval, construct source-anchored probes, and run one deletion-and-reanswer for probe-linked entries. Combine those measured flips with retrieval/citation traces to train an operation-conditioned memory-utility critic and to settle online ordinal entry credit that is propagated through retained version chains as an action-level proxy reward.

memory_design.write: A Qwen3-8B policy chooses Write, Merge, or Noop for event and profile layers while a verbatim layer losslessly preserves every turn; destructive deletion is excluded from the evaluated policy.
memory_design.organize: Entries live in event/profile/verbatim layers; Merge appends a new version while retaining older versions. The learned policy tends to consolidate same-topic facts into multi-version chains, but the interface provides the version structure.
memory_design.read: Management uses deterministic top-4 retrieval per managed layer; answering uses a cross-layer top-10 plus one provenance-expansion step. Retrieval logs and answer-time citations form the observational audit trail used for credit.
memory_design.update_forget: Merge creates non-destructive version chains and the learned policy adapts which facts to merge. The paper deliberately avoids destructive forgetting, so deletion rights, retention budgets, and long-term revocation remain outside the demonstrated lifecycle.

compared_to: Outcome-only GRPO under the same memory scaffold, retrieval stack, answerer, and judge
Observational attribution without the intervention-calibrated flip/toxicity branches
Matched-scale, shuffled-flip, flip-only, toxicity-only, and critic ablations
SFT/untrained same-scaffold managers plus reproduced external memory systems for system-level context
analysis.evidence: On held-out LoCoMo, the same-scaffold ladder goes from 58.6 untrained to 62.5 SFT, 63.4 outcome-only GRPO, 70.2 observational attribution, and 77.5 for the full method. The final two ladder arms differ only in intervention-calibrated flip promotion and toxicity terms, adding 7.3 points beyond observational attribution; matched-scale and shuffled-flip controls stay near 70.5. The full 2x2 shows approximately additive critic and audited-term effects. On LongMemEval, the ladder is 66.0 outcome-only, 72.5 observational, and 79.0 full. The audit also verifies that deleting 74.6% of entries outside every logged read path changes accuracy by only -0.1 points, while deleting cited entries costs 12.4 points.
analysis.why_it_matters: This is a stronger causal template for memory learning than rewarding a packaged trajectory: it asks whether a specific persisted entry changes a fixed downstream reader, then uses that intervention to supervise the memory-management policy. The next benchmark for learned memory writers should distinguish entry-presence counterfactuals, action-level credit, and total supervision cost instead of treating episode reward as component evidence.
limitations: The controlled deletion establishes entry-presence utility for a fixed answerer/prompt/decoding setup, not the ideal per-action difference reward; version-chain propagation is an approximation and sampled action-level replay reports Spearman 0.72.
The storage schema is domain-coupled: direct LoCoMo-to-LongMemEval transfer falls to 58.4, while schema adaptation without policy retraining reaches 71.2 versus 79.0 native training.

The evaluated store is lossless and intentionally avoids destructive forgetting or hard retention budgets, so overwrite, revocation, privacy deletion, and bounded-storage behavior are not established.

Offline supervision is expensive: three LoCoMo seeds use about 1.6M API calls (~$1,100), and the LongMemEval experiment about 9.8M calls (~$6,500); this cost must be charged against outcome-only or simpler writer baselines.
